intro_html: If you have ever wanted that tangy, peppery Italian beef without the sandwich shop price, this is your recipe. One chuck roast and a jar of pepperoncini turn into fourteen hearty rice bowls with a little kick. Set it in the morning and dinner is basically finished by the time you are.
cost_closing_html: About $3.62 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot of finished beef and peppers, subtract the empty pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. Give each container that same scoop over an even bed of rice and beans so no bowl comes up short.
upsell_html: That is fourteen warm, satisfying Italian beef bowls from one roast and a jar of peppers, at a fraction of the cost of takeout. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Watch for chuck roast markdowns. This cut is your cheapest path to fourteen filling dinners. Buy it when the price drops and freeze it until slow cooker day.
One jar of pepperoncini does the heavy lifting. The peppers and their juice are the whole flavor of this dish, and a jar is cheap and keeps forever in the fridge.
Green peppers are cheapest in season. Bell peppers get pricey in winter, so buy them when they are low and even freeze extras sliced. Frozen peppers work great cooked right into the beef.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot on a kitchen scale and write the number down. You will need it to portion evenly at the end.
Cut the chuck roast into large chunks, season with a little salt and pepper, and place them in the slow cooker.
Pour in the whole jar of pepperoncini along with its juice, add the beef broth, sliced yellow onion, minced garlic, and Italian seasoning. Give it a stir.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours, until the beef shreds easily with a fork.
Shred the beef right in the pot with two forks and stir it back through that tangy pepper broth so every bite soaks up the flavor.
Cook your rice per the package, warm and drain the black beans, and slice the green bell peppers to stir in during the last stretch of cooking.
Build each bowl with rice on the bottom, a scoop of the beef and peppers, beans, and a little reduced fat mozzarella on top so it melts into the warm meat.

head.description: A high-protein Italian meal prep. Fourteen servings at about 504 calories and 36 grams of protein for roughly $3.62 each (at everyday cost).
